what: Westlake makes chemicals and building products: PVC and the chlorine and ethylene that go into it, plus pipe, siding, windows and roofing made from the same materials.
customers: Builders, pipe manufacturers and industrial chemical buyers in North America, Europe and Asia.
money: pipe, fittings, siding, windows and roofing
moat: Integration from chlorine and ethylene all the way to finished building products, which captures margin at every step and uses cheap American natural gas as the feedstock.
risks: A $447M net loss as chemical prices fell and the housing market stayed weak
$6.4B of debt, though against $2.7B of cash
opportunities: Analysts see about 30% upside, with 17 covering the stock
The building products half is far steadier than chemicals and has held up through the downturn
Cheap American natural gas gives its chlor-alkali plants a structural cost advantage over European rivals
watch: PVC prices and whether housing construction recovers.
